items.body:
OpenAI模型或完成百万美元千禧年大奖杨米尔斯问题的一半证明

11 月 12 日，据 MTS 发文，OpenAI 的人工智能模型已证明物理学领域一项百万美元千禧年大奖问题的一半，并由诺贝尔奖得主领衔的评审组予以支持。MTS 称，该问题即杨-米尔斯问题。OpenAI 于 10 月 26 日首次公布相关证明，并表示其模型在 9 月完成了这项工作。

据 MTS 介绍，评审组由诺贝尔奖得主 David Gross 担任主席，成员包括曾共同撰写该千禧年大奖问题官方表述的 Arthur Jaffe。相关证明还已用可逐行核验的计算机语言 Lean 完成形式化。杨-米尔斯问题是 2000 年设立的七大千禧年大奖难题之一，每项奖金 100 万美元；迄今唯一被解决的一项由格里戈里·佩雷尔曼完成，但其本人拒绝领取奖金。

MTS 指出，要赢得该奖项，仍需证明质量间隙，并满足克莱数学研究所关于发表及经过两年认可期的规则。X 用户 Theo Jaffee 表示，物理学家已能在经验层面处理量子场论和量子杨-米尔斯理论，但一直缺少对这套理论为何成立的数学形式化。

items.body:
谷歌也加入决策模型大战：支持五种模态，成本是Jev的两倍多

谷歌发布首款决策模型 Gemini Decision 1，支持文字、图片、音频、视频和 PDF 混合输入，25.6 万 Token 上下文。

相比 Jev 和 OpenAI Decisions API，谷歌能直接处理更多类型的材料。比如把一段客服录音、订单信息和商品照片一起交给模型，同时判断客户诉求、问题严重程度及是否需要人工介入。

一次最多判断 1000 个问题，多个问题共用同一份材料，只需支付一次材料的输入费用。官方公布的端到端响应时间为 150 至 250 毫秒。在 1.6 万 Token 以内，问题从 1 个增加到 100 个，模型计算耗时基本不变。

谷歌自测中，Gemini Decision 1 在 JevBench 上拿到 92.2%，超过 Jev 1.14 的 90.0% 和 OpenAI Decisions API 的 90.9%。但在工具调用评测 When2Call 上，谷歌以 79.9% 落后 Jev 的 82.0%。

第三方 Artificial Analysis 的 Decision Index v2.1 中，Gemini Decision 1 综合得分 65.98，在 18 款模型中排第九，与 Jev 的 66.23 基本持平，落后榜首 Drex Max v1.1 的 72.62。

谷歌每百万输入 Token 收费 0.1 美元，输出免费。按 Artificial Analysis 的统一任务组合计算，每完成 100 万项任务，谷歌约需 345 美元，Jev 仅需 156 美元，Drex Max 约 103 美元。谷歌平均每项任务耗时 211 毫秒，Jev 则为 92 毫秒。

谷歌已将新模型用于 Gemini Notebook 的模型路由，部分日常请求延迟最高降低 40%。API 现已开放，提供免费测试额度。

items.title: 美联航限制AI智能体订票 CEO直言“不想再多一个中间商”
items.summary: 美国联合航空周三宣布，将采取措施限制未经授权的第三方个人AI代理或助手访问其服务，涉及自有数字平台，以及通过旅行社和聚合平台进行的间接访问。美联航称，此举旨在保护旅客账户、敏感信息及交易安全，并防范自动化操作可能带来的合规风险。 据悉，AI代理仍有途径向消费者展示美联航的航班选择和价格，但将无法在其网站上代为完成交易。在安全和合规考量之外，美联航首席执行官斯科特·柯比也直言存在商业层面的顾虑。“坦白说，我不想再创造一个中间商。”柯比周二在芝加哥的一场活动上表示。 —— 财联社、彭博社

items.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI
items.summary: A conversation with Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer at Gilbert + Tobin.
items.body:
November 12, 2026

A conversation with Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer at Gilbert + Tobin.

Read the case study

Company size: Enterprise

Region: Asia-Pacific & Oceania

Products: ChatGPT, Codex

Industry: Services

Our Executive Function series features perspectives from leaders driving transformation through AI.

Gilbert + Tobin⁠(opens in a new window) is one of Australia’s leading corporate law firms, with work spanning capital markets, mergers and acquisitions, disputes, and technology. The firm operates in a profession built on specialist knowledge, careful judgement, and the secure handling of sensitive information.

Gilbert + Tobin began by giving its people room to experiment with AI, then introduced ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Work and Codex to move from individual assistance to defined, multistep agentic workflows, with people responsible for review and approval.

We spoke with Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer at Gilbert + Tobin, about leading adoption from the front, where he’s seeing the value of AI, and his advice for other CEOs.

We have three objectives: to use AI to deliver better services to our clients, make Gilbert + Tobin a great place to work for our people and firmly establish ourselves as a leader in our market.

The real value we’ve seen from AI so far hasn’t been about reducing cost or needing fewer people, but freeing our people to focus on the more human side of their work, meeting with clients, coaching their teams and mentoring the future leaders of our industry.

“It’s been about…freeing them up to then do the more human side of their work.”

—Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer, Gilbert + Tobin

When ChatGPT first became available, we encouraged people to experiment with it and think about where it might create value. We were clear that no client data or confidential information should be entered. That gave people a safe, constrained environment to experiment.

The next step was to provide a secure channel to powerful AI. We introduced ChatGPT Enterprise in a controlled environment and expanded from there. Australian data residency, contractual protections, role-based access and administrative controls gave us the confidence to scale while meeting our requirements and those of our clients.

Governance should enable responsible use. Our message was simple: AI is not cheating. It is another tool people can use to apply their judgement. They still need to define the task, check the output and take responsibility for the final work.

Leaders have to use the technology themselves: experiment, push the boundaries and learn what works. When people see that AI matters to you, it sets the tone and encourages others to engage with it.

We did not mandate usage targets. Instead, we made the technology relevant. Our business transformation team demonstrated workflows tailored to different functions, while videos, showcases, challenges and an early AI bounty surfaced ideas from across the firm.

Gilbert + Tobin has always been willing to lean into new technology. What has been most encouraging is the creativity coming from every part of the organisation – not only the technology team.

“Getting started yourself…sets the tone and encourages others.”

—Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer, Gilbert + Tobin

To help manage my workload more effectively, I created a “digital twin” through a custom GPT (now shifting to Plugins) using examples of my writing, feedback I had received, context about the firm and the way I like to work. It started as a tool for me and became more valuable when I shared it with my direct reports.

My team is now able to use it to get “my feedback”, effectively, via ChatGPT. It lets them test their thinking against my context and working style before coming to me. It does not make decisions or speak for me; it helps our conversations start from a stronger place.

I also used ChatGPT Work in a confidential annual review process involving our 120 partners. I asked it to update files with data from a spreadsheet, create PDFs and bundle the finished material. It completed the work in minutes.

With a product as powerful as ChatGPT Work, it’s important to have the right admin controls behind the scenes, and it now provides detailed, granular data on usage. When I checked the usage dashboard afterwards, the cost for that annual review work was about $62. That was a good trade for the time I saved – and for work that would otherwise have required several other people over multiple days.

Start by using the technology yourself. Experiment with real work, understand its limitations and show your people that learning matters.

Pair that leadership with clear governance and practical enablement. Give teams examples tailored to their roles, create safe ways to test ideas and keep people responsible for the result.

The opportunity is bigger than doing the same work a little more quickly. Used well, AI can raise the quality and volume of what an organisation produces – and give people more time for the complex, strategic work where their expertise and judgement create the greatest value.

We have three objectives: to use AI to deliver better services to our clients, make Gilbert + Tobin a great place to work for our people and firmly establish ourselves as a leader in our market.

items.title: Supporting research on AI and children’s safety
items.summary: OpenAI commits $2 million to research on AI and children’s safety. The work supports shared tools to measure risks and opportunities for young people.
items.body:
November 12, 2026

Global Affairs

Supporting research on AI and children’s safety

OpenAI pledges $2 million as part of a global effort to better understand AI’s impact on children and support their safety and wellbeing.

Earlier this week at the Paris Peace Forum, OpenAI signed the Charter of Engagement for Safer AI for Children⁠(opens in a new window) and committed $2 million to support the scientific research network under the Coalition for Children’s Rights and Protection in the Age of AI.

This builds on our call for global standards on youth AI safety, and sustained collaboration among governments, researchers, civil society and industry to translate shared evidence into practical safeguards.

Our contribution supports shared measurement work: developing tools researchers can use to better understand and measure AI’s risks and opportunities for children, helping inform safer products and better policy.

The charter sets out shared principles for safe, age-appropriate AI, alongside a research programme and safeguards for its independence. Research teams retain control over their conclusions, and findings will be published, including negative or inconclusive results.

This work will help build the evidence needed to support the benefits of AI for young people while addressing risks to their safety and development. It builds on our support for comprehensive youth AI safety legislation that establishes strong, enforceable protections while preserving access to tools for learning, creativity and opportunity. Such frameworks should include age-appropriate safeguards by default, tools for parents, regular risk assessments and mitigation, and meaningful accountability. We look forward to engaging with European policymakers as the EU Kids Act develops, and with partners around the world to advance stronger protections and opportunities for young people.

items.title: ChatGPT Ads increases its market presence in 44 countries
items.summary: Aleph selected as ChatGPT Ads’ exclusive reseller in 44 countries to offer local invoicing, in-person support and local market expertise to brands and agencies
items.body:
November 12, 2026

ChatGPT Ads increases its market presence in 44 countries

Aleph selected as ChatGPT Ads’ exclusive reseller in 44 countries to offer local invoicing, in-person support and local market expertise to brands and agencies

Starting today, brands and agencies in 44 countries can contract, pay and get local support for ChatGPT Ads through Aleph, OpenAI’s exclusive reseller. Aleph offers local advertisers in these countries an additional buying option alongside our existing global technology partners⁠ and our self-service ChatGPT Ads Manager⁠(opens in a new window).

The reseller agreement covers advertisers based in the following 44 markets:

• Latin America (14): Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Puerto Rico and Uruguay

• Europe and Central Asia (16): Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Hungary, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Ukraine* and Uzbekistan

• Middle East and Africa (10): Egypt, Kenya, Kuwait, Morocco, Nigeria, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates

• Asia-Pacific (4): Bangladesh, Cambodia, Hong Kong* and Sri Lanka

Today’s announcement does not impact any advertisers ability to target any of these countries in a campaign. Advertisers globally can continue to create and run campaigns targeting any country where ChatGPT Ads are available⁠(opens in a new window).

Advertisers and agencies in these markets who are interested in buying ChatGPT Ads from a local entity or local salesforce, can contact Aleph’s local teams⁠(opens in a new window) to learn more. Aleph offers local contracting and invoicing in local currency, payment terms, onboarding, campaign support and training.

Advertisers and agencies interested in buying ads directly can continue to buy through Ads Manager. Advertisers and agencies interested in buying through global technology partners in these markets can continue to do so.

Over one hundred thousand marketers have advertised on ChatGPT, and we continue to improve the platform based on what we learn from people and businesses. Today’s announcement represents additional local ways to purchase ChatGPT Ads across these markets.

We’ve made significant progress in ten months, but we are still early in building the full potential of ChatGPT Ads. As we expand into new markets, and develop new formats, optimization tools, and measurement solutions, we’ll remain focused on broadening access to powerful AI, protecting the trust people place in ChatGPT, and helping businesses achieve their goals.

Author

OpenAI

*OpenAI models and ChatGPT are not available to users in mainland China or Hong Kong, so ChatGPT Ads are not available in-market. Businesses based in these markets can advertise to ChatGPT users in markets where Ads are available through authorized advertising partners, subject to applicable eligibility requirements.

items.title: 因地图问题 多个中国品牌手机在越南下架
items.summary: 11月4日起，越南多家电子零售商因收到内部紧急指令，将华为、OPPO、小米、荣耀、传音、努比亚和魅族等中国品牌手机从展柜撤下，并暂停相关品牌二手回收及销售业务。据业内人士分析，问题疑似源于部分中国品牌手机预装的天气应用，其在海外版中仍保留了含非法地图信息的组件，严重侵犯越南主权。目前，小米和荣耀已完成软件更新并重新上架。OPPO方面则回应称其天气应用使用The Weather Channel服务，未发现地图合规问题，部分零售商撤柜仅为预防性措施。预计相关机型将在数日内陆续恢复展出。 —— VnExpress International
items.body:
因地图问题 多个中国品牌手机在越南下架

11月4日起，越南多家电子零售商因收到内部紧急指令，将华为、OPPO、小米、荣耀、传音、努比亚和魅族等中国品牌手机从展柜撤下，并暂停相关品牌二手回收及销售业务。据业内人士分析，问题疑似源于部分中国品牌手机预装的天气应用，其在海外版中仍保留了含非法地图信息的组件，严重侵犯越南主权。目前，小米和荣耀已完成软件更新并重新上架。OPPO方面则回应称其天气应用使用The Weather Channel服务，未发现地图合规问题，部分零售商撤柜仅为预防性措施。预计相关机型将在数日内陆续恢复展出。

—— VnExpress International

👁️ 英伟达董事会据称准备罢免黄仁勋，另有公司女高管为三者

英伟达董事会正准备罢免首席执行官黄仁勋，并计划最早于当天召开会议，讨论其去留问题。此前，黄仁勋被曝涉及两段婚外关系，其中一名女性被美国方面怀疑与中国情报机构有关，另一名则是英伟达内部高管。

这一系列丑闻使黄仁勋面临前所未有的管理层和公司治理压力。黄仁勋此前已承认对妻子不忠，英伟达董事会也已启动独立调查。消息传出后，英伟达股价盘后大幅下跌约 8%。不过，英伟达尚未对此作出正式回应。
